label: prop:neutron-proton-mass-splitting
title: Neutron--proton mass splitting from quark crossing change
html:
The neutron--proton mass difference is

  \Delta m
  = m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}}
  = \alpha \cdot
    \bigl\lvert
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}) -
      \Phi(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d})
    \bigr\rvert
  \approx 1.302 \;\mathrm{MeV}

where \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the binding scale and \Phi is the quantum dilogarithm volume.

Proposition (in the convention-C trace frame). The traced-volume closed form behind \Phi folds the Markov parameter into its integer coefficients as z = 4993/10000, the rounded z_C = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) = 0.4993203342 at q_0. The canonical frame is z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) = 0.6126880371, and carrying z_D through the same closed form moves \lvert\Delta\Phi\rvert by -19.01\%, giving \Delta m \approx 1.054 MeV against CODATA 1.29333217 MeV — a residual of -18.5\% where the z_C value above sits at +0.64\%. The figure 1.302 MeV is therefore a statement in the z_C frame.

That is a claim about this construction in this frame, and not an exclusion: nothing here shows a quark-ordering volume cannot carry the splitting. Nor is the closer z_C agreement evidence for z_C, since it was obtained in the frame the framework does not use, and a trace convention is not something a residual may select.
